meta.title: DIP-I-496: show role and permission for a logged-in user
meta.prompt: Propose a design for this ticket: DIP-I-496

source.title: Show role and permission for a logged-in user
source.body: As a logged-in user I want to see which permission group I belong to, so that I know what I am allowed to do in the catalog and where to read the guidelines for it. Today the group is only visible to an administrator, in the Users table in Administration. Group names are set when the group is created and are often technical keys, so the group needs a separate readable name that an administrator can set. Note that a user can hold more than one group, and that a group can grant access in one catalog and not in another.

context.question: What does a user see about their permission group?
product: A user can belong to several groups.
Group names are technical keys that scripts reference.
A group may grant access in one catalog only.
context.gap: The account menu has no capture in app-context.

goals: A user reads their group from the account menu.
A group carries a readable name.
nonGoals: Assigning groups; that stays in Administration.

research.skippedBecause: the evaluation names the decisions first; research runs against them on resume

openQuestions.text: Whether a readable name is set once for the group or per catalog.
A person in many groups needs a rule for how many the account menu lists before it truncates.

decisions.question: How does a user see which group they belong to?
